definitions.explanation: Shutting someone up in a room or building and not letting them out, typically a deposed ruler, a rival, or a captive. A written word, common in history and fiction.

examples.english: The king was locked away in a tower.
The princess was confined deep inside the castle.

examples.japanese: ⟦{権力|けんりょく}→権力：10020_kenryoku⟧⟦{争|あらそ}い→争い：09992_arasoi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{敗|やぶ}れた→敗れる：12712_yabureru⟧{皇子|おうじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{遠|とお}い→遠い：00529_tooi⟧⟦{島|しま}→島：00885_shima⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{屋敷|やしき}→屋敷：12395_yashiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{幽閉|ゆうへい}⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧まま⟦{一生|いっしょう}→一生：01728_isshou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{終|お}えた→終える：02019_oeru⟧。
examples.english: The prince who lost the power struggle spent the rest of his life confined in a mansion on a distant island.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幽閉|ゆうへい}⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧: to be locked away (the usual form)
- ⟦{塔|とう}→塔：09944_tou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{幽閉|ゆうへい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to imprison in a tower
- {幽閉|ゆうへい}⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧: life in confinement

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{監禁|かんきん}→監禁：13647_kankin⟧: confinement as a crime, the word in police reports and the news. {幽閉|ゆうへい} belongs to history and storytelling: rulers and nobles shut away by their enemies.
